question: Which elementary cellular automata bind a cell's future to its past in knots (minimal decisive sets of two or more cells, by TIME-KNOTS-20261107-001A's Theorem 1), and how do those knots behave as the lag T grows?

public_inputs.rules: The 88 classes of elementary rules under reflection and complement, each by its least member.
public_inputs.lags: T = 1 to 6 (the T-step map on 2T + 1 cells, at most 13).
public_inputs.measures: For each rule and lag: whether the map is constant; the number of knots and of ties; the knot sizes (cells + 1); whether the cell's own past value (cell 0) lies in a knot; the least knot through it; whether the map is a single term or clause.
public_inputs.classes of behaviour: knot-free at every lag (only ties or constant); exactly one knot at every lag; knots at every lag whose number grows with T; anything else, listed.

forbidden_inputs: Changing rules, lags or measures after seeing results
primary_observable: The partition of the 88 rules into the declared classes of behaviour over T = 1..6, with each rule's knot counts and least knot sizes.
cheapest_meaningful_control: Linear rules 60, 90 and 150 must show exactly one knot at every lag, of the size Theorem 3 gives; rule 128 (AND) and rule 254 (OR) must be knot-free with 2T + 1 ties; every knot-free map must be a term or a clause (Theorem 2). A census that fails these is not read.
decision_or_followup_rule: Report the partition. If some rule is knot-free at small lags but not at larger ones, list it with the first lag that has a knot. If the least knot through the cell's own past grows like T + 2 for all non-linear rules with knots, record that as the pattern; otherwise list the exceptions.
stop_rule: Stop at T = 6 for all 88 rules.
nonclaims: Exploratory and non-promotable: lags up to 6 only.
Two-time knots only: knots through intermediate rows are not counted here.
No claim about Wolfram's classes beyond the comparison stated.
feasibility_disclosure: Before freezing: ticket A's library was written and checked (its check.py), including rules 60, 90, 150, 128, 254, 30, 110 and 184 at T = 1 to 5 while sizing (rule 30: 2, 2, 9, 22, 36 knots; rule 110: 3, 4, 9, 18, 31; rule 184: 3, 10, 35, 126, 462). The decisive-set table takes under a second per rule at 13 cells. No full census was run.
